subject: Marketplace packaging and channel carveout question: seat vs usage (AWS/GCP)
messages:
From: Amit Patel <amit@orbital-analytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudWave Reseller <rev@cloudwave.io>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Packaging question — seat vs usage + channel margin carveout for AWS/GCP private offers

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency numbers. We are discussing two different packaging approaches internally and wanted to get your recommendation and an operational example for a Private Offer on AWS and a GCP marketplace listing:

Options we're considering:
- Flat seat-based subscription (e.g., 50 seats/month) billed via Private Offer
- Pure usage (tokens/sec or vCPU-hours equivalent) billed via marketplace usage reports
- Hybrid (base seat + overage usage)

Key asks from our procurement and channel team (CloudWave, reseller):
1) Can Redwood support an explicit channel margin carveout in a Private Offer so the reseller still sees a bundled list price and keeps a fixed % margin?
2) How would invoicing and settlement work if we use AWS Private Offer vs GCP Marketplace?
3) Any recommended list-price anchoring and SKU mapping patterns — we need to preserve channel economics while keeping unit economics predictable.

We can share a preliminary forecast if that helps. Also looping in CloudWave (cc) since they want to confirm margin treatment.

Thanks,
Amit Patel
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Orbital Analytics

Attachments: forecast_Q1_Q3.csv (3 months forecast)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Amit Patel <amit@orbital-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging question — seat vs usage + channel margin carveout for AWS/GCP private offers

Hi Amit — great to hear from you and glad the numbers resonated. Short answers up front, then details and next steps below.

Short answers:
- Yes, we can structure Private Offers to preserve a reseller margin via list-price anchoring + pass-through line items.
- AWS Private Offer and GCP Marketplace have different settlement semantics; both can work but ops steps differ.
- Recommended: a hybrid SKU model (base seat SKU + per-token SKU) to keep list-price visible to the channel while capturing usage economics.

Details and operational notes:
- Channel carveout approach: create a composite listing where the visible list price to the buyer includes the reseller margin. Redwood records show the allocation of revenue and the underlying net price to Redwood. The reseller can be paid via a pass-through invoice or via cloud marketplace payout depending on the marketplace.
- AWS specifics: Private Offer allows you to set a negotiated list price per SKU. The reseller (CloudWave) can receive a separate commercial arrangement from you; AWS will bill Orbital at the negotiated list price. For payout to CloudWave, you can either (a) pay them outside AWS (recommended for speed) or (b) use AWS partner billing features if you want programmatic pass-throughs.
- GCP specifics: Marketplace typically uses list-price SKUs and Google handles payouts to partners where configured; however, GCP has stricter SKU and metering requirements so SKU mapping is important.

I'm attaching an initial SKU mapping (redwood_sku_mapping_v3.xlsx) and a draft private offer template (oa_private_offer_template.docx) showing line-item examples and how margin appears on the buyer invoice.

Next steps:
1) Ben — can you propose a channel margin waterfall (tiered) we should present to CloudWave?
2) Soojin — can you confirm operational steps for ingesting a GCP metered SKU vs an AWS Private Offer (DocuSign/process owners and expected timeline)?
3) Amit — if you can confirm expected commit (monthly ARR or tokens/month) we'll draft a sample Private Offer and run the numbers.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if helpful.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_sku_mapping_v3.xlsx, oa_private_offer_template.docx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Patel <amit@orbital-analytics.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging question — seat vs usage + channel margin carveout for AWS/GCP private offers

Putting some numbers behind the margin request — thinking out loud:

Proposed waterfall (example):
- List price visible to buyer: $12,000/month (composite: base seat SKU $8,000 + usage buffer SKU $4,000)
- Target CloudWave margin: 15% of list -> $1,800/month
- Redwood net after channel: $10,200/month
- If usage exceeds the buffer, overage SKU priced at $0.00012/token (net) with a tiered rebate to CloudWave on high-volume months.

Operational asks for the quote:
- We need a 12-month commit anchor to make the margin predictable for CloudWave.
- Please confirm whether Orbital prefers invoicing cadence monthly or quarterly for budget approvals.

A couple of gotchas:
- For GCP, if you expose many metered SKUs you increase operational complexity; prefer a consolidated metered SKU per model family if possible.
- For AWS Private Offers we can make the list price look like a single line item; CloudWave can get their margin via a separate reseller agreement outside AWS.

If Amit can confirm monthly commit (or an ARR target), I'll prepare a sample pricing sheet and include a revenue waterfall and example payout schedule for CloudWave.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Director, Channel Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Amit Patel <amit@orbital-analytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging question — seat vs usage + channel margin carveout for AWS/GCP private offers

Hi Ben / Hannah — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers and a small update:

1) We expect to land on a hybrid model: 40 seats (+ base support) and an estimated 35B tokens/month as overage buffer for Q1.
2) Monthly invoicing is preferred (finance wants predictable monthly charge).
3) CloudWave confirmed they need a visible 15% margin on the buyer invoice; they are okay with receiving their margin via a separate monthly payment from Orbital outside the cloud marketplace (simpler for their ops).

I've attached the forecast (forecast_Q1_Q3.csv) with month-by-month tokens and seat counts. We are comfortable with the waterfall example Ben provided; please go ahead and produce the sample pricing sheet + DocuSign-ready Private Offer.

One last ask: can Redwood include an explicit line in the Private Offer that documents the reseller as "Commercial Partner — CloudWave" for audit clarity? CloudWave asked for that.

Thanks,
Amit

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Packaging question — seat vs usage + channel margin carveout for AWS/GCP private offers

Thanks all — operational checklist and next steps below. I also added a DocuSign draft link to the sample Private Offer.

Operational checklist (high level):
1) SKU mapping finalization — Hannah/Ben to confirm which model families map to the consolidated metered SKU. (target: 2 business days)
2) Draft Private Offer & DocuSign — I'll load the OA-specific values (list price, line items, partner name) and share for signature. DocuSign draft: https://www.docusign.com/oa-proposal-draft
3) CloudWave payment flow — because Orbital prefers external payment to the reseller, we'll include language in the offer referencing "Commercial Partner — CloudWave" and note that reseller commission will be paid directly by Orbital under a separate reseller agreement.
4) GCP metering — I will work with the billing team to provision a consolidated metered SKU; expect 5–7 business days for validation on GCP. For AWS Private Offer, we can provision the Private Offer within 48 hours once the DocuSign is signed.

Deliverables I'll provide: sample pricing sheet, DocuSign Private Offer draft, and an ops-runbook for month-end settlement for CloudWave.

Amit — I took your forecast and will use the Q1 numbers for the first-pass pricing; Ben will get the waterfall embedded in the sheet. Expect the first draft by EOD Wed.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Marketplace Ops Lead | Redwood Inference
